title: Is the square root of 2 a fraction?

probes.question: What is the first move in a proof by contradiction?
options: Assume the statement is true and stop

probes.question: True or false: if the square root of 2 equalled a/b, then a squared would equal 2 times b squared.

image.alt: A Babylonian clay tablet (YBC 7289) with a square and its diagonals, inscribed with an ancient approximation of the square root of 2.
image.credit: Urcia, A., Yale Peabody Museum of Natural History, http://peabody.yale.edu, http://hdl.handle.net/10079/8931zqj derivative work, user:Theodor Langhorne Franklin

body.question: Can the square root of 2 be written exactly as a fraction of two whole numbers?
body.reveal: No. Suppose it were a/b in lowest terms. Then a squared equals 2 times b squared, so a is even. Write a as 2k and the same steps show b is even too. But a fraction in lowest terms cannot have both even. That is proof by contradiction: assume the opposite and reach an absurdity.
